fit.text: JavaScript applications and concise functional scripting.

prerequisites.text: Install Node.js for the CLI and learn LiveScript's function and operator syntax.

costs.text: The MIT-licensed compiler is separate from Node and imported JavaScript libraries.

implementation.name: Logtalk with a supported Prolog backend
implementation.version_scope: Documentation as checked on 2026-10-13; no latest-version claim.

fit.text: Organize Prolog applications with objects, protocols and reusable categories.

prerequisites.text: Learn Prolog facts and rules before Logtalk message sending and object interfaces.

execution.text: A supported Prolog backend executes compiled Logtalk objects.

behavior.text: Objects encapsulate predicates; calls use the object::message notation.

tooling.text: The project includes many runnable examples and portable tools.

maintenance.text: Backend selection matters; test features against the supported Prolog implementation.

costs.text: Logtalk's Apache license is separate from the Prolog backend's license.

example.code:
:- object(hello).
    :- public(say/0).
    say :- write('PLLDN'), nl.
:- end_object.
example.run_instructions: In a Logtalk-enabled Prolog session, load hello.lgt with logtalk_load(hello), then query hello::say.

implementation.name: Mercury compiler with native C backend
implementation.version_scope: Documentation as checked on 2026-10-13; no latest-version claim.

fit.text: Typed declarative applications combining logic and functional programming.

prerequisites.text: Learn predicates, modes and determinism; IO states are explicit.

execution.text: mmc --make builds an executable from a named Mercury module.

behavior.text: Modes and uniqueness express data flow, including ordered I/O effects.

tooling.text: The compiler builds module interfaces and intermediate files automatically.

maintenance.text: Track the selected backend grade and module dependencies for reproducible builds.

costs.text: Compiler COPYING contains GPL version 2; runtime and libraries need independent component checks.

example.code:
:- module hello.
:- interface.
:- import_module io.
:- pred main(io::di, io::uo) is det.
:- implementation.
main(!IO) :- io.write_string("PLLDN\n", !IO).
example.run_instructions: With Mercury and its required backend compiler installed, run mmc --make hello, then run hello.

behavior.text: Each dispatched compute thread operates on its grid index.

example.run_instructions: Use Apple's calculation sample as the host, bind equally sized buffers to slots 0-2, select add_values and dispatch one thread per element. Shader source alone is not a standalone application.
example.expected_result: For one input element 2 and one input element 3, the output buffer contains 5 after GPU completion.

implementation.name: libminizinc compiler and configured solver
implementation.version_scope: Workflow follows the versioned MiniZinc 2.10.0 handbook.

fit.text: Scheduling and discrete constraint models solved by a chosen backend solver.

prerequisites.text: Learn finite variable domains, constraints and a solve item.

execution.text: minizinc compiles a model, calls its solver and formats a solution.

behavior.text: A satisfy model requests a feasible assignment, rather than a fixed imperative execution order.

tooling.text: The IDE and CLI both accept model and data files.

maintenance.text: Solver choice and search behavior matter; keep model and solver versions together.

costs.text: libminizinc uses MPL-2.0 except marked files; solver and IDE licensing is separate.

example.run_instructions: With MiniZinc and a compatible configured solver installed, run minizinc sum.mzn.
example.expected_result: Returns x = 2 with a solution separator.
